subject: Critical Thinking
subcategory: Evidence & Truth: How We Know What's Real
title: The Map Is Not the Territory
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Map Is Not the Territory usable.

hook.text: Alfred Korzybski said: 'The map is not the territory.' Your model of reality is not reality itself.

buildup.text: Every theory, model, & belief is a simplification of reality. Useful simplifications – but simplifications nonetheless.

discovery.text: All maps distort. The Mercator projection makes Greenland look as big as Africa. Africa is 14 times larger.

twist.text: The danger: mistaking the model for reality. Economists treat markets as rational.

climax.text: George Box: 'All models are wrong, but some are useful.' Use models, but never worship them.

punchline.text: Your model works — until it doesn't. Stay ready to redraw the map.

quiz.question: What does 'the map is not the territory' mean?
options: Our models and theories are useful simplifications, not reality itself
We should only trust direct experience

details.summary: Alfred Korzybski's principle reminds us that our models, theories, and mental representations are simplifications of reality, not reality itself. No map captures every feature of the territory it represents.
details.whyItMatters: Confusing the map for the territory leads you to trust models too much, miss details they omit, and forget that reality is always more complex than any representation.
takeaways: All models are simplifications that omit some features of reality
Useful models capture the most relevant features for a purpose
Mistaking models for reality leads to overconfidence and surprise

faq.question: How does the map-territory distinction apply to everyday thinking?
faq.answer: Your mental model of a friend, your financial plan, and your understanding of politics are all maps. They simplify reality to be useful. Remembering they are incomplete prevents you from being blindsided by details your model omitted.

faq.question: What makes a good map if no map can be perfectly accurate?
faq.answer: A good map captures the features most relevant to your current purpose while clearly acknowledging what it leaves out. A subway map is excellent for navigation but terrible for geography. Fitness for purpose is the standard.
